title: What does NFTokenMint do on XRPL?
abstract: Sourced explanation of NFTokenMint and its practical limits.
body:
According to XRPL documentation, NFTokenMint creates an XRPL non-fungible token with issuer-chosen properties. [1]

Flags determine capabilities such as transferability or issuer burn rights, while URI points to associated information rather than storing a whole artwork on the ledger. An authorized minter can act for an issuer under the documented arrangement. Minting proves creation of a token identifier, not copyright ownership or the truth of external metadata. [1]

The NFTokenMint reference defines the operation-specific fields alongside the shared XRPL transaction fields. Account identifies the submitting account; signing authority, transaction cost and sequence handling still have to satisfy the ledger rules. A submitted transaction or an example in documentation does not establish a successful validated result. Where an amendment is required, confirm it is enabled on the intended network before relying on the feature. [1][2]

Author interpretation: before using NFTokenMint, compare the intended change with the current ledger state and keep the transaction hash with the resulting metadata. Treat unresolved outcomes as unresolved; submitting a replacement operation can create a second obligation. These are integration recommendations, not a report of a live test. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
